Excellent!
Sep 2026 • Couples
We had dinner here our first night in Tunis and it was a wonderful surprise.
Although the location is very simple and not particularly well-kept, it was a wonderful dinner thanks to the excellent food and service.
We ordered their typical fried appetizers, which arrived along with olives, Harissa, and ricotta offered by the house. We continued with the couscous; both the lamb and the chicken were special!
The staff was very kind in explaining everything to us. Very fair price, about €15 per person.

Pretty good
Apr 2026 • Solo
Well, I'll be honest, the food is excellent quality but it's not my style. There we are on a refined modern cuisine like gourmet restaurant and moreover most of the customers who were there that day were tourists. 

So it's modern cuisine, and I'm a traditionalist and I want to stay that way. I took grilled fish (you can't go wrong about this kind of food, you know in advance what to expect), well no. 

Typically, when grilled fish are taken, it is expected that there will be one whole fish on the plate. There was only one portion. The person who was there took care to tell me twice that it was toasted girl so we have nothing to blame them on this point. But the fries and mayonnaise were missing. Who can imagine grilled fish without fries or mayonnaise? Instead, I was served stir-fried vegetables, which is good for you, but we're used to fries, whatever you want. 

And then there was this black and white rice... in cuttlefish ink I was told! Cuttlefish ink in rice, we Tunisians haven't really used it, I would have preferred a portion of couscous. 

I give five stars even for the quality of the service, after all it is not their fault that I came to a restaurant that is not my style, I am sure it will please quite a few people.

The best restaurant in Tunis
Feb 2026 • Couples
Whoa! Whoa! Whoa! We found our safe haven in this restaurant, as we are intolerant to spices and Tunisian cuisine is full of them: exquisite food; barely mentioned spices; choices of various dishes and impeccable service.
It's a bit more expensive than the others but the location and location (very close to Place de la Victoire and Bab al Bhar) are great for those who don't want to venture into the Medina at night or want to avoid the horrible restaurants of Avenue Bourguiba.
During Ramadan they offer a special menu but the à la carte menu allows both to choose from a set menu and freely.
The place is quiet, the food really nice and exquisite and the bread they offer is sublime.
Straconsigliato if you want to eat Tunisian cuisine without running into spicy food.

A friendly,professional, reasonably priced and reliaby good restaurant in the heart of Tunis.
Jan 2026 • Couples
We came here on the basis of the reviews which it certainly lived up to; we came four times and only not on our last night as they're closed on Sundays.Interestingly other couples were also repeat customers. 
We did a recce on arrival in Tunis and were warmly welcomed by the two young men who were on front of house every day.A good sign.
There are a couple of starters and a dozen or so mains,allowing for three different types of couscous for example and variations of pasta dishes,fresh fish ,perhaps four desserts but we got addicted to the chocolate fondant-an absolutely first class pudding.No alcohol, but an alcohol free beer,lemonade and tea/coffee and we honestly didn't miss it.
The set menu is seductive and good value but was too much food for us and after the first attempt we found a main course and the chocolate fondant was ample. 
Attractive surroundings,some modern art and nice crockery.
Really excellent all round.Very good food at reasonable prices.Payment in cash in dinars,euros or sterling.
